brief: Create a single hollow 3D-printable lower-leg part, 330 mm tall, shaped like a human calf and shin: broad and rounded near the upper calf, bulging slightly backward, tapering gradually into a narrow ankle, with a gently curved front shin surface and smooth anatomical contours. Upper cross-section 115 × 105 mm, lower 85 × 80 mm, with 8 mm walls. Add a 210 × 60 mm rectangular opening on the back with six 4.5 mm mounting holes for a removable lid. Add reinforced 12 mm-thick hinge tabs at the top and bottom, each extending 37.5 mm beyond the body with a centered 8.5 mm pivot hole running left to right.

requirements.statement: The overall finished part shall stand 330 mm tall.
The upper calf cross-section shall be 115 mm in its wider in-plane dimension.
The upper calf cross-section shall be 105 mm in its other in-plane dimension.
The lower ankle cross-section shall be 85 mm in its wider in-plane dimension.
The lower ankle cross-section shall be 80 mm in its other in-plane dimension.
The shell wall shall be 8 mm thick throughout the body.
The rectangular opening on the back shall be 210 mm along its longer dimension.
The rectangular opening on the back shall be 60 mm along its shorter dimension.
Each of the six lid mounting holes shall be 4.5 mm in diameter.
The hinge tabs at top and bottom shall be 12 mm thick.
Each hinge tab shall extend 37.5 mm beyond the body.
Each hinge tab shall have a centered pivot hole 8.5 mm in diameter running left to right.
The part shall have exactly six mounting holes on the back opening for the removable lid.
requirements.rationale: Brief states six 4.5 mm mounting holes for the lid.

requirements.statement: The part shall have exactly two pivot holes, one on each hinge tab (top and bottom).
requirements.rationale: One hinge tab at top and one at bottom, each with a centered pivot hole.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 6 open holes of 4.5 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

requirements.statement: Each 4.5 mm hole shall cut only the wall the brief puts it on, not run on through the facing wall.
The part shall have 1 opening 210 by 60 mm through its wall.
The floor shall be 8 mm thick.

assumptions.statement: The part is 3D-printed in a common FDM thermoplastic (e.g., PLA or PETG) at standard indoor ambient conditions, with no special temperature or chemical exposure.
assumptions.rationale: Brief specifies '3D-printable' but no material grade or environment.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Wrong material choice could affect strength, especially at hinge tabs if any load is applied.

assumptions.statement: The 8 mm wall thickness applies uniformly to the entire shell body, and the hollow cavity is a constant offset of the outer anatomical contour.
assumptions.rationale: Brief states '8 mm walls' with no variation specified.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If walls were meant to vary by region, the part may be heavier or weaker than intended in places.

assumptions.statement: The removable lid itself is out of scope for this part's requirements; only the opening, its mounting holes, and their count/size on this shell are specified here.
assumptions.rationale: Brief does not give the lid's thickness, material, or exact hole layout -- only the opening size and hole count/diameter on the shell.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a mating lid part is expected to be generated with matching features, this scoping choice would need revision.

assumptions.statement: The six 4.5 mm mounting holes are plain clearance holes for self-tapping screws or bolts, not threaded or fitted with inserts.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives only a diameter, not a thread callout or insert specification.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If threaded holes or heat-set inserts were intended, the hole feature and any wall allowance around it would need to change.

assumptions.statement: The 8.5 mm pivot holes are plain through-holes for a pin or axle, with no bushing, bearing, or wear insert.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives only a hole diameter and orientation ('running left to right'), with no bushing or bearing callout.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the hinge is meant to carry repeated motion under load, a bare printed hole may wear quickly or fail.

assumptions.statement: The transition between the 115x105 mm upper cross-section and the 85x80 mm lower cross-section is a smooth continuous loft/taper, with the broader/rounded bulge biased toward the back (posterior) near the top and a gently curved front (anterior) shin face, per the brief's anatomical description.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives only two cross-sections and a qualitative shape description; the full profile between and beyond them must be interpolated.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A different interpolation could change wall-to-wall clearance or anatomical likeness, though it would not violate the two stated cross-sections.

assumptions.statement: Part height (330 mm) runs along the Z axis; 'left to right' for the pivot holes is interpreted as the X axis, 'front/back' as the Y axis, with the opening on the -Y (posterior) face.
assumptions.rationale: Brief uses anatomical terms (front, back, left-right) without defining a coordinate frame.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the assembly's reference frame differs, hole axis and opening face would be mis-oriented relative to mating parts.

unknowns.question: What connects to the pivot holes at the hinge tabs (pin/axle material and diameter tolerance, and what structure is on the other side of each hinge -- e.g., a knee joint above, a foot/ankle joint below)?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Without knowing the mating hardware, the pivot hole's fit, retention method, and tab reinforcement adequacy cannot be assessed.
unknowns.suggested_default: 8.5 mm hole sized for an 8 mm steel pin with clearance fit, retained by E-clips

unknowns.question: If the hinge is functional (not just decorative), how many pivot cycles is it expected to endure over its service life?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Fatigue life of printed hinge tabs under repeated motion depends heavily on cycle count, which cannot be assumed.

notes: REQ_WALL_THICKNESS was bound to `parameter:wall_thickness`; `wall_thickness` is a measurement of the part, not a dimension the design declares, and the claim is now measured as it says.
dropped 2 load question(s): the brief names no load, force or margin -- it describes a shape, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

added REQ_HOLES_4_5MM: the brief states 6 open holes of 4.5 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_4_5MM_ONE_WALL: the brief puts 4.5 mm holes on one face of a hollow part, and a hole drilled with no depth runs on through the facing wall -- the right number of holes, the right size, half of them on the wrong side. Counted on the part: the walls each cuts.
added REQ_OPENINGS_210X60: the brief gives openings a length and a width -- slots, not holes of one diameter -- and nothing counted them. Counted on the built part, laid flat, by their size.

REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_Z held the whole part to 330 mm along z, but the brief puts something beyond the body and gives no height for the whole part: 330 mm is the body's, and the part is at least that. No design could have met it as it was.

added REQ_FLOOR_THICKNESS at 8 mm: the brief describes a container -- 8 mm walls, a 8 mm floor -- and a solid block, a sealed hollow box and the part asked for all have the same bounding box. Each is measured on the built part through its middle, from the side it is open on.

document.name: Lower-leg shell
document.description: Hollow, 3D-printable lower-leg (calf/shin) shell lofted from an upper and lower rectangular cross-section, with a rear access opening and lid mounting holes, and reinforced hinge tabs with pivot holes at top and bottom.

parameters.description: Height of the main body (hinge tabs extend beyond this)
Hinge tab footprint width (top tab reuses this; set from lower section as a conservative, defensible value since brief gives no separate tab width)
Distance from top of body to top edge of rear opening, chosen to centre the opening region along the back (assumption, not in brief)
Inset of mounting holes from the opening edge

interfaces.description: 210x60 mm rear access opening mated by a removable lid (lid is out of scope)
Bottom hinge tab pivot bore, left-right axis
Top hinge tab pivot bore, left-right axis
